review_status: draft v1 - surf and inlet coastal species

profile.diet: Mole crabs (sand fleas), coquina clams, shrimp, and small crustaceans
profile.behavior: Fast coastal swimmer that feeds in the surf break, sandy troughs, and tidal inlet currents.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, ideal for surf-feeding pompano.
factors.value_notes: The aquaculture/life-history synthesis reports Florida pompano avoid water below about 20 °C, with mortality at 10–12 °C; spawning, larval development, and juvenile growth are reported optimal around 25–30 °C. These are physiological and early-life-stage data, not a calibrated adult surf-zone catch curve. They support the broad 18–30 °C range but do not validate the 22–27 °C ideal for adult fish.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in the shallow surf and trough zone.
factors.value_notes: FWC reports inshore/nearshore habitat along sandy beaches, oyster bars, and seagrass, with records to about 40 m. The life-history synthesis describes juveniles using beach surf zones and moving offshore when water falls below 20 °C. This supports shallow coastal use but not the exact 0.5–20 m / 1–8 m ideal across seasons and life stages. Depth is an active gate.

value_text.peak: It is peak pompano surf-run season.
value_text.off: It is outside the main pompano surf run.

factors.value_notes: FWC reports spawning offshore March–September and temperature-influenced seasonal movement; the life-history synthesis suggests southeastern U.S. spawning February–October with peaks April–May and September–October, while Gulf/Caribbean spawning may occur year-round. The configured March–May and October–December window may represent seasonal Florida availability, but is not a validated monthly catch curve.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.
text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
